reviewedBoundaries: Commands.run preserves an existing timeout/command/observation error while recording later snapshots, owned-group cleanup, flush/close/digest/stat/capacity and persistence errors separately.

Every command starts one owned session. Only that PID/PGID is signaled; process snapshots never authorize signaling service PIDs. Six existing helper bodies remain exact; terminate_owned differs only signature and two signal-recording calls.

Creation captures the original fresh UUID into memory and a context/source-bound journal before later group finalization. Recovery rechecks the original intent/baseline/start record/argv/cwd/log hash; unknown creation is INCOMPLETE.

The original exact UUID query remains30seconds. Exactly its TimeoutExpired plus a timely exact-group ESRCH permits one separately labeled120second read-only observation; original failure remains the primary and overall failure.

Qualified shutdown/delete cleanup is attempted independently in main finalization, with one durable claim preventing repeated attempts. Missing/unfinished ownership or cleanup is never treated as absence.
1200second global admission reserves240seconds for cleanup/source finalization; per-command and output accounting remain finite. Output limits are explicitly sampled, not hard quotas.
The standalone workflow and central inline packet are parsed-equivalent after removing only the route condition.

environmentPreflight.finding: Apple documents print-path as the active directory and DEVELOPER_DIR as its per-process override. The script inherits the environment and requires the exact override. No demonstrated need for global --switch.

limitations: No simulator command, diagnostic, product test, App build, native build or repository import ran in this review.
Process samples may miss ancestors/descendants and cannot establish service causation.
Synchronous filesystem calls are not a hard global process deadline; the finite workflow step remains an outer limit.
A durable result written before a subsequent restoration/unlock error may be superseded by compact final stdout and nonzero actual exit; both originals must be retained.
